subject: Business
title: Blue Ocean Strategy
description: A quick, practical guide to Blue Ocean Strategy.

hook.text: Cirque du Soleil didn't compete with other circuses. It created an entirely new market space.

buildup.text: Blue ocean strategy means creating uncontested market space instead of fighting in bloody red oceans.

discovery.text: Red oceans are crowded markets where everyone competes on the same dimensions. Blue oceans redefine the game.

twist.text: Blue oceans don't stay blue forever. Success attracts imitators who turn any blue ocean red over time.

climax.text: Nintendo Wii targeted non-gamers with motion controls while Sony and Microsoft fought over hardcore gamers.

punchline.text: Stop competing where everyone else is. Compete where nobody is.

quiz.question: What is a 'blue ocean' in business strategy?
options: An uncontested market space with no direct competition
A market dominated by a single company
A market that is shrinking rapidly

details.summary: Blue ocean strategy creates uncontested market space by making competition irrelevant rather than fighting for share in crowded existing markets. Developed by Kim and Mauborgne, it uses value innovation to simultaneously pursue differentiation and low cost.
details.whyItMatters: Most companies compete in red oceans of fierce rivalry. Blue ocean strategy provides a framework for escaping price wars and finding new demand, which has been applied successfully by companies from Cirque du Soleil to Nintendo Wii.
takeaways: Blue oceans are new market spaces where competition is irrelevant
Value innovation pursues differentiation and low cost simultaneously
The strategy canvas tool visually maps competitive factors to find gaps

faq.question: How did Cirque du Soleil create a blue ocean?
faq.answer: Cirque eliminated costly circus elements like animals and star performers while adding theater, artistic music, and storylines from Broadway. It created a new entertainment category that attracted adults willing to pay premium prices, avoiding competition with traditional circuses.

faq.question: Is blue ocean strategy applicable to small businesses?
faq.answer: Yes. Small businesses often find blue oceans by combining elements from different industries, serving overlooked customer segments, or reimagining delivery channels. The framework scales from solo entrepreneurs to Fortune 500 companies.
